mainTopic: Doubtfully prepared food on יום טוב: trapped animals, and gifts a גוי brings on יום טוב.
overview: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב one may slaughter animals already held in enclosures, but not animals found in nets or traps, since they may have been caught on יום טוב itself. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds a distinction: traps found sprung before יום טוב mean the animals are permitted, and traps found sprung on יום טוב mean they are forbidden. The גמרא resolves an apparent contradiction between his two clauses: any case of doubt is treated as caught on יום טוב and is forbidden. שמואל rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's fish that a גוי brought to רבן גמליאל. רב says they are permitted only to be received, and לוי says they may even be eaten. רב explains that both views come from רבי, who changed his ruling overnight, and that לוי missed the morning session. A ברייתא about 'same-day' produce turns out to mean food that only looks freshly picked. Finally, רב פפא rules that a גוי's gift is forbidden if that kind of produce is still growing. If nothing of that kind is still growing and the gift came from inside the תחום, it is permitted. His ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Enclosures are permitted, traps are not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that animals from enclosures may be slaughtered on יום טוב, but not animals found in nets or traps.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may slaughter animals taken from enclosures on יום טוב, but not animals taken from nets or traps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets the basic rule: animals already held in an enclosure may be slaughtered on יום טוב, but animals sitting in hunting nets or traps may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals in an enclosure were already caught and ready before יום טוב began. An animal in a trap might have been caught on יום טוב itself. Catching it then was forbidden, and it was not 'ready' (מוכן) when the day began, so the ברייתא forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Enclosures or pools where animals are already confined

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the background rule that an animal must be 'ready' before יום טוב. The rest of the סוגיא asks how to handle cases where we don't know when the animal was caught.

phrases.english: One may slaughter from the enclosures on the Festival,
phrases.notes: These animals were already caught and confined before יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מִן הָרְשָׁתוֹת וּמִן הַמִּכְמוֹרוֹת.
phrases.english: but not from the nets or from the traps.
phrases.notes: They may have been caught on יום טוב itself.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals from enclosures may be slaughtered on יום טוב. Animals from nets or traps may not, because they may have been caught on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: it depends when the trap was found sprung
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that traps found sprung before יום טוב mean the animals are permitted, and traps found sprung on יום טוב mean they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: if he came and found the traps sprung on ערב יום טוב, we know the animals were caught before יום טוב, and they are permitted. If he came and found them sprung on יום טוב, we know they were caught on יום טוב, and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר divides the trap case into two situations, based on when the person saw that the trap had caught something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trap was already sprung before יום טוב, the animal was clearly caught then, so it was ready and is permitted. If he checked the trap just before יום טוב, found it untouched, and then found it sprung on יום טוב, the animal was clearly caught on יום טוב and is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Disturbed or sprung, a sign that an animal was caught
It is known, it is clear

steps.confusionAlert: Here מקולקלין does NOT mean the meat is spoiled. It means the trap is 'messed up' (sprung or disturbed), which shows that an animal got caught in it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא וּמְצָאָן מְקוּלְקָלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: If he came and found them sprung on the eve of the Festival —

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁמֵּעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב נִצּוֹדוּ, וּמוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: it is known that they were caught on the eve of the Festival, and they are permitted.
If he came and found them sprung on the Festival —
phrases.notes: For example, he checked just before יום טוב and found the traps intact.

phrases.english: it is known that they were caught on the Festival, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a more detailed position to the ברייתא's trap case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Traps found sprung before יום טוב: the animals are permitted. Traps found sprung on יום טוב: the animals are forbidden.

steps.title: First clause implies that a doubt is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge: the first clause stresses that the trap was 'found sprung', which implies that if we are unsure, the animals are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא contradicts itself. You said: if he came and found them sprung on ערב יום טוב, it is known they were caught before יום טוב. The reason is that he actually found them sprung. That implies that in a case of doubt, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge against the ברייתא from within. This step only sets up the first side, an inference from the first clause. The clash comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause permits only when he actually saw the trap sprung before יום טוב. The גמרא reads this precisely: the permission depends on certain knowledge. So if we don't know when the animal was caught, it should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא וּמְצָאָן מְקוּלְקָלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: If he came and found them sprung on the eve of the Festival —
it is known that they were caught on the eve of the Festival.
The reason is that he came and found them sprung,
but in a case of doubt, they are forbidden.
phrases.notes: An inference drawn from the precise wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the precise wording of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's first clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first clause of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The precise wording implies that a doubt is forbidden. This becomes one side of an internal contradiction.

steps.title: Second clause implies that a doubt is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge: the second clause stresses that the trap was 'found sprung on יום טוב', which implies that a doubt is permitted. This contradicts the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now read the end: if he came and found them sprung on יום טוב, it is known they were caught on יום טוב. The reason is that he actually found them sprung then. That implies that in a case of doubt, we assume they were caught before יום טוב, and they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the second clause the same precise way and gets the opposite result. Now the two clauses clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If forbidding requires certain knowledge that the animal was caught on יום טוב, then a doubtful case should be permitted. So the first clause says a doubt is forbidden, and the second says a doubt is permitted. The ברייתא seems to contradict itself.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
If he came and found them sprung on the Festival —
it is known that they were caught on the Festival.
The reason is that he came and found them sprung,

phrases.aramaic: הָא סְפֵיקָא — מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב נִצּוֹדוּ, וּמוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: but in a case of doubt, they were caught on the eve of the Festival, and they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction begun in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read precisely, the first clause makes a doubt forbidden and the second clause makes a doubt permitted. Both cannot be true.

steps.title: Reading the second clause as 'treated as caught on יום טוב'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא means a doubtful case is treated as if the animal was caught on יום טוב, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if he came and found them sprung on ערב יום טוב, it is known they were caught before יום טוב, and they are permitted. But in a case of doubt, it is treated as if they were caught on יום טוב, and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by explaining how to read the ברייתא. Only a trap seen sprung before יום טוב is permitted. Every doubtful case counts as 'caught on יום טוב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause's inference stands: a doubt is forbidden. The second clause is not limited to certain cases. Its 'known to be caught on יום טוב' really means 'treated as caught on יום טוב', and that includes doubtful cases. So the second clause no longer implies that a doubt is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (a re-reading of the source)
It becomes like, it is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, an animal in a trap is permitted only if the trap was clearly sprung before יום טוב. If we are unsure, it is forbidden.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא וּמְצָאָן מְקוּלְקָלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: If he came and found them sprung on the eve of the Festival —

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁמֵּעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב נִצּוֹדוּ, וּמוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: it is known that they were caught on the eve of the Festival, and they are permitted.

phrases.aramaic: הָא סְפֵיקָא — נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁנִּצּוֹדוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וַאֲסוּרִין.
phrases.english: But in a case of doubt, it is treated as if they were caught on the Festival, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 3–4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second clause forbids only when we know for sure the animal was caught on יום טוב, so a doubt would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second clause includes doubtful cases, which are treated as caught on יום טוב. So a doubt is forbidden, in line with the first clause.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר as just explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, an animal found in a trap may be slaughtered on יום טוב if the trap was seen sprung before יום טוב. If there is any doubt about when it was caught, it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading early אמורא in בבל

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: animals from traps found sprung before יום טוב are permitted. If there is any doubt, they are treated as caught on יום טוב and are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule that when we are unsure whether something was ready before יום טוב, we are strict.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the position explained in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: trapped animals are permitted only if they were clearly caught before יום טוב, and a doubtful case is forbidden.

steps.title: What does 'permitted' mean in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's words in the משנה, 'they are permitted,' and asks what exactly is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he said: They are permitted.' Permitted for what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about the fish a גוי brought to רבן גמליאל on יום טוב and asks what 'permitted' actually means. This sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מותרין' is vague. It could mean permitted to take and move, or permitted to eat. The גמרא wants to pin down how far the permission goes.

phrases.english: And he said: They are permitted.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. רבן גמליאל is speaking about the fish brought by the גוי.

phrases.english: Permitted for what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on a different line of the משנה, after the traps discussion concluded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far the permission of 'מותרין' extends: only receiving and moving, or also eating.

steps.title: רב and לוי disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב says the fish are only permitted to be received. לוי says they are even permitted to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They are permitted to be received. And לוי said: They are permitted to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question. רב says you may only accept the gift. לוי says you may even eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, you may take the fish and move them, but you may not eat them on יום טוב, since they may have been caught that day. According to לוי, even eating is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav said: They are permitted to be received.
phrases.notes: Receiving and moving only. Eating is not allowed.

phrases.english: And Levi said: They are permitted to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with two opposing views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: permitted only to receive and move. לוי: permitted even to eat.

steps.title: Never miss the study hall, even for a moment
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a person should never keep himself away from the בית המדרש, even for one moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A person should never keep himself away from the study hall, even for one moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב states a general life lesson. He will prove it in the next step with the story behind his dispute with לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This lesson is tied directly to the dispute above. רב is about to explain that he and לוי disagree only because לוי missed one session.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A person should never hold himself back
from the study hall, even for one moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a lesson that will explain where the רב–לוי dispute came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should never be absent from the בית המדרש, even briefly.

steps.title: רב's story: רבי changed his ruling overnight
steps.stepSummary: רב tells how רבי first said the fish may be eaten, then the next morning said they may only be received. רב was there and changed his view. לוי was absent and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For לוי and I were before רבי when he said this teaching. In the evening he said: They are permitted to be eaten. In the morning he said: They are permitted to be received. I, who was in the study hall, changed my view. לוי, who was not in the study hall, did not change his.
steps.whatsHappening: רב proves his lesson with a personal story. The story also explains why he and לוי ended up disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views come from רבי. 'Permitted to eat' was רבי's first ruling, and 'only to receive' was his final ruling. לוי missed the morning session, so he kept teaching the earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I retracted; I changed my view

steps.confusionAlert: לוי is not inventing his own opinion. He faithfully reports רבי's first ruling. רב's view matches רבי's final ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's position, 'only to receive,' reflects רבי's later and final ruling.

phrases.english: For Levi and I were before Rabbi
when he said this teaching.
In the evening he said: They are permitted to be eaten.
In the morning he said: They are permitted to be received.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא — הֲדַרִי בִּי.
phrases.english: I, who was in the study hall, retracted.

phrases.aramaic: לֵוִי דְּלָא הֲוָה בִּי מִדְרְשָׁא — לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Levi, who was not in the study hall, did not retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the lesson of step 9 and explains the source of the dispute in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The lesson never to be absent from the בית המדרש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's eyewitness account of רבי's evening and morning rulings.

steps.title: Challenge to לוי from a ברייתא about fresh produce
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a gift from a גוי is permitted, even very fresh fish and same-day produce. That fits רב, but how can same-day produce be permitted to eat, as לוי would say?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If a גוי brought a gift to a Jew, even very fresh fish and same-day produce are permitted. That works well for the one who says 'permitted to be received.' But for the one who says 'permitted to be eaten': is same-day produce allowed to be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks לוי's view using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce picked on יום טוב is forbidden to eat, since it was attached to the ground when the day began. So 'permitted' in the ברייתא seems to mean only 'permitted to receive.' That matches רב and contradicts לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A gentile who brought a gift to a Jew,
even moist, fresh fish
and produce of that same day: they are permitted.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוּתָּרִין לְקַבֵּל — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'permitted to be received,' it is fine.
But according to the one who says 'permitted to be eaten,'

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירוֹת בְּנֵי יוֹמָן מִי שָׁרוּ בַּאֲכִילָה?
phrases.english: is same-day produce permitted to be eaten?
phrases.notes: Picked on יום טוב, so it was attached to the ground when the day began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the רב–לוי dispute against a ברייתא, targeting לוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that the gift is permitted to be eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits same-day produce. Such produce cannot be eaten on יום טוב, so 'permitted' must mean only receiving.

steps.title: Counter-question: can same-day produce even be moved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around: by your logic, same-day produce should not even be allowed to be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning: is same-day produce permitted to be moved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the challenge works against רב just as much as against לוי. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce picked on יום טוב is מוקצה, so even moving it is forbidden. So the ברייתא cannot mean real same-day produce even under רב's view. That means the challenge proves nothing against לוי.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירוֹת בְּנֵי יוֹמָן מִי שָׁרוּ בְּטִלְטוּל?
phrases.english: is same-day produce permitted to be moved?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Neutralizes the challenge of step 11 by showing it equally troubles רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that the ברייתא supports רב over לוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Real same-day produce is מוקצה and may not even be moved, so the ברייתא cannot mean it under either view.

steps.title: The ברייתא means produce that only looks freshly picked
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of fish with red gills and produce kept fresh in greens. It is called 'same-day' only because it looks that fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are dealing with fish whose gills are still red and produce preserved in greens. Why is it called 'same-day'? Because it is like same-day produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא is really talking about, so it no longer contradicts לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food was not actually caught or picked on יום טוב. It was only kept fresh. So it is not מוקצה and may even be eaten, which fits לוי. The challenge falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: רב says the gift may only be received; לוי says it may be eaten. Both views come from רבי: his first ruling allowed eating, and his final ruling allowed only receiving. The ברייתא about 'same-day' produce refers to food that only looks freshly picked, so it fits both views.

phrases.english: Rather, with fish that are red
phrases.notes: Their gills are still red, so they look freshly caught.

phrases.english: and produce preserved in greens are we dealing.
And why does it call them 'of that same day'?
Because they are like produce of that same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּכְווֹרֵי דַּאֲדִימֵי וּפֵירֵי דִּכְבִישִׁי בְּיַרְקָא עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading of the ברייתא after step 12 showed the literal reading fails for everyone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא meant produce actually picked on יום טוב, which supports only receiving.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means produce that was not picked on יום טוב but only looks that fresh. It is not מוקצה and may even be eaten, so it fits לוי.

steps.title: רב פפא's ruling when the same kind of produce is still growing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if a גוי brings a gift on יום טוב and that kind of produce is still attached to the ground, it is forbidden. It stays forbidden after יום טוב for the amount of time it would take to pick it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is that if a גוי brought a gift to a Jew on יום טוב, and some of that same kind of produce is still attached to the ground, the gift is forbidden. Even in the evening after יום טוב, it is forbidden for the amount of time it would take to pick it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the final, practical ruling for a gift brought by a גוי on יום טוב. This ruling covers the case where the same kind of produce is still growing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא argued about how fresh the gift looks. רב פפא gives a clearer test: is this kind of produce still growing in the field? If it is, we suspect the גוי picked it today, which is a מלאכה done for the Jew. So the Jew may not use it on יום טוב, and even after יום טוב he must wait as long as it would take to pick it, so he gains nothing from the forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law; the final ruling we follow
Still attached to the ground or tree, still growing
For the amount of time it would take to do the work (here, to pick it)

steps.confusionAlert: Waiting until nightfall is NOT enough. Even after יום טוב ends, you must also wait the time it would take to pick the produce. That way you get no benefit from the work the גוי did on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the whole discussion about gifts from a גוי on יום טוב. It replaces the vague question of how fresh something looks with a simple test.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: the halacha is:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁהֵבִיא דּוֹרוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: a gentile who brought a gift to a Jew on Yom Tov,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין בִּמְחוּבָּר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: if there is some of that same kind still attached to the ground, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: We assume the גוי picked it today.

phrases.english: And in the evening too, they are forbidden for the time it would take to make them (pick them).
phrases.notes: So the Jew gains no benefit from the work done on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was explained (red gills, produce kept fresh in greens), רב פפא gives the practical ruling for the whole topic.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If that kind of produce is still growing, a גוי's gift on יום טוב is forbidden. It stays forbidden after יום טוב until enough time has passed to have picked it.

steps.title: רב פפא's ruling when none of that kind is still growing
steps.stepSummary: If none of that kind of produce is still attached to the ground, and the gift came from inside the תחום, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if none of that kind of produce is still attached to the ground, then if it came from within the תחום, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues his ruling with the opposite case, where nothing of that kind is still growing. This passage ends here, but his ruling continues with the case of a gift from outside the תחום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing of that kind is still growing, it could not have been picked today, so there is no problem of picking. If the gift was also brought from inside the תחום, no forbidden travel happened either. So there is no problem at all, and it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside the limit (about 2,000 אמות past the town) that one may walk on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא checks two things: (1) Is that kind of produce still growing? If so, it is forbidden. (2) If not, where did it come from? From inside the תחום, it is permitted. The outside-the-תחום case comes next.

phrases.english: And if none of that same kind is still attached to the ground,
if it came from within the techum, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: No picking and no forbidden travel were involved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's ruling with the opposite case, where nothing of that kind is still growing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With nothing of that kind still growing, a gift brought from inside the תחום is permitted on יום טוב.
